notes.title: Update Notes for August 9, 2023
notes.notes:
Updates:
1. Flame thrower buff - If flamethrower plume is held on a single target for a period of time, adds a small amount of extra damage which increases over time. resets that extra damage if plume isn't hitting target for 1 second. Extra damage shown in cyan color
2. Flashlight Wide Mod - When using Flashlight Kill Beam with Wide Mod, increases the Flashlight kill beam width with a unique effect

Fixes:
1. Tech Drop - Tech drop cannot be selected when level is ending to prevent loss of tech drop
2. Fix for not being able to shoot properly after hitting escape from Menu in-game

notes.title: Update Notes for August 3, 2023

[olist]

notes.title: Patch Notes for July 11, 2023
notes.notes:
Bug Fixes: 
1. Fix for Tutorial where ammo was not being given to player when needed
2. Buttons 'Alt' and 'Ctrl' no longer shoot as they were not intended to be mapped

Gameplay changes:
1. Data Modules now give Merc Cred to the team when picking them up. Player picking up the module gets 400 Merc Cred, other team members get 250 Merc Cred. We hope that this will drive players to focus on getting the modules when playing, and perhaps drive some friendly competition to get to them first.

UI Changes:
1. Current and Total Health are both displayed as X / X on the player UI now. Makes it easier to know the diff between your current and max health, especially after getting a max health upgrade

notes.title: Update Notes for Dec 21, 2021
notes.notes:
[list]
[*] Added Partial Controller support for Xbox controllers. Xbox controller can now be used to navigate most pre-game menus and some in-game UI menus. XBox controller works for all in-game movement, shooting, radial menus, etc. We will continue to view feedback and make improvements to the UI navigation and in-game controls for the XBox controller.
[*] Made the score multiplier more visually interesting.
[*] Fixed bug where players would take damage from poison spit when having poison heal perk

notes.title: Release Date Annoucement
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings Mercenaries! [/h1]
 
[h2]Release Date [/h2]
 
We are incredibly excited to announce our release date for Flashlight is now set for October 26th!
 
[h3]The Journey [/h3]
 
It’s been over a year and a half since this project first began. It’s been a life-long dream of our team to create and release a video game. There were some previous solo attempts with individuals on our team, but they never made it far beyond the initial sparks of enthusiasm. Aside from the many technical skillsets it takes to complete a game, it also requires will, determination, and some grind. In our experience, those things are a lot easier to maintain if you have at least one or two others who can help maintain the excitement and enthusiasm. Fortunately, we had that this time around. 
 
The initial concept of our game was inspired, in large part, by an old game called “Armor Critical” (a.k.a. ARC). This was a major childhood favorite of our developer Rich Muhlenkamp and his friends. It was mainly a top-down multiplayer capture the flag game. The simple fun mechanics were incredibly easy to pickup and enjoy but took a surprising amount of skill to master. Rich wanted to bring some of those experiences back to life with a new flavor: a co-op experience, and the ability to play solo if desired. 
 
[h2]Flashlight [/h2]
 
Flashlight is multiplayer at its core. With both PvP and Co-op, Flashlight allows friends to join up and either compete head-to-head or cooperate together within its procedurally-generated levels and terrain in story mode. Both can be played solo (bots available in Pv P modes), but we believe it shines most when played with friends. 
 
[h3]PVP [/h3]
 
Players can join rooms of up to 12 players to battle it out in Capture the Flag or Team Deathmatch modes. It will initially be released with 9 different PVP maps; 5 maps supporting 4 simultaneous teams and 4 maps supporting 2 simultaneous teams. Teams will fight it out to either capture enough flags to win the round, or be the first to reach 25 kills in Team Deathmatch. More game modes and maps hopefully to come after release! 
 
[h3]COOP [/h3]
 
The story mode in Flashlight allows for up to 4 players to journey together along the procedurally-generated terrain fighting hordes of zombies and enemy mercenaries to uncover the secrets of the infection. There are 4 playable mercenary groups. Each group has a different set of perks that can be selected as you rank up along the way, giving a variety of builds and a different flavor on each play through. This mode is a rogue-lite type of experience. You will probably die a lot and don’t expect to beat it the first time!  
 
[h2]Final Thoughts [/h2]
 
We are thrilled to finally release Flashlight to the world! It’s a life-long dream borne into reality after two years of hard, but fun and rewarding, work. Thanks to everybody who helped and supported us, and to those who wishlisted our game. We hope everybody enjoys it. Your feedback is always appreciated and we will try to make improvements, and hopefully additional features, based on that feedback. 
 
And again, stay safe and keep the lights on!
